text: The Wyrmwood reserve has reintroduced the red squirrel, according to a statement on Tuesday from the reserve’s director, Elin Voss, and a briefing note filed with the Department for Wildlands Conservation. The first 18 animals were released on 14 October after a six-month acclimatisation programme, with a further 12 expected next spring if monitoring remains favourable. Ms Voss said the species had been absent from the 4,200-hectare reserve for more than 40 years, largely because of habitat loss and competition from grey squirrels. The department’s note said early signs were “encouraging,” citing feeding activity and two confirmed nesting sites near Alder Hollow.
